data.name: Jadab
data.gender_notes: Jadab is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit root ‘jada’, meaning ‘not dry’ or ‘tender’. In Hindu mythology, the name Jadab is associated with Lord Shiva, representing the gentle and loving aspect of the deity. The name Jadab carries the meaning “Gentle, tender, loving” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jadab usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, tender, loving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jadab belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, tender, loving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jadab total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jadab holds significant cultural importance as it is derived from the Sanskrit language, which is the primary language of Hindu religious texts and philosophy. In Hindu culture, names have deep meanings and are often believed to influence the personality and destiny of the individual. The name Jadab reflects the tender and gentle nature, which is a valued trait in Hindu society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jadab holds deep significance as it is associated with Lord Shiva, the god of destruction and regeneration in Hindu mythology. The tender and loving aspect of Lord Shiva depicted in the name Jadab highlights the belief that even the most destructive forces in nature have a tender and loving side. The name Jadab is also believed to bestow the blessings of Lord Shiva upon the individual, providing them with strength, protection, and the ability to overcome challenges in life.

The name signifies the preservation of one's roots, traditions, and spiritual lineage.
